video_caption: The video opens with a static graphic featuring a vintage, newspaper-style design on a beige, textured background. At the top left, a smaller box displays "PechaKucha 20x20 IMAGES SECONDS PechaKucha.org DEVISED & SHARED BY KLEIN DYTHAM ARCHITECTURE." Centered at the top, larger text reads "PechaKucha Night CALGARY 20x20 IMAGES SECONDS." A green banner on the left side is marked "EVENT #35." The most prominent feature is the large, distressed, dotted font text in the center stating "OVERDUE." Below this, a green banner declares "In partnership with ROCKET HOUSE & CALGARY PUBLIC LIBRARY." At 00:08, the screen splits vertically; the right side retains the vintage graphic design but now displays "KIMBERLY A. WILLIAMS" in the same retro font, while the left side reveals a woman with dark, curly hair tied back, wearing glasses and a black top, standing at a microphone on a stage with a blurred, colorful cityscape backdrop. She looks down at a paper on the podium, smiling slightly, before beginning to look up towards the audience.

In this video segment, a woman with dark curly hair, wearing glasses, a black top, and a dark scarf, stands at a wooden podium with a microphone, presenting information. Behind her, a stylized cityscape with illuminated buildings serves as a backdrop. On the right side of the screen, presentation slides are displayed, providing visual context to her speech.

At the beginning, the slide shows the title, "The Best and Worst Places to be a Woman in Canada 2017," with the subtitle "The Gender Gap in Canada's 25 Biggest Cities," and author "Kate McInturff," under the "Canadian Centre for Policy Alternatives, October 2017." The presenter notes that Calgary ranks 22nd among Canada's 25 largest metropolitan areas.

The slide then transitions to display "Ranking based on:" followed by bullet points: "Educational Attainment," "Economic Security," "Personal Security," and "Health Status," as she explains these are the areas of research.

As she discusses educational attainment, the slide changes to a visual representing education: a blackboard with faint mathematical equations, a stack of three books, and a white mug filled with colorful pencils, with a pair of round black glasses resting on the top book. She highlights that women in Calgary are more likely than men to have completed high school, college, or university, with 28% holding university degrees.

Finally, the slide shifts to a screenshot of a "CALGARY HERALD" news article titled "Calgary rated one of worst Canadian cities for women workers in pay equity and employment," dated October 13, 2016. She points out that despite high educational attainment, Calgary ranks poorly in gender pay equity. Throughout her presentation, she gestures with her hands to emphasize her points.

A woman with short, curly brown hair and glasses, dressed in a black top and dark necklace, stands behind a podium speaking passionately into a microphone, using hand gestures to emphasize her points. The background behind her features an abstract, colorful illustration resembling a city skyline at night. In the upper right corner of the screen, a news headline from the "Calgary Herald" reads: "Calgary rated one of worst Canadian cities for women workers in pay equity and employment." Below the headline, the author is identified as "MICHELE JARVIE, CALGARY HERALD" and the update date is "October 13, 2016." Further below, a URL for the accessed article is provided. The woman continues to speak, maintaining a serious and engaged expression as she elaborates on the issues related to women's employment and pay equity in Alberta.

A woman with brown, curly hair and glasses, wearing a black top, stands behind a podium with a microphone, gesturing with her hands as she speaks. Behind her is a background depicting a city skyline with warm, glowing lights. To the right, the screen displays several slides throughout her speech. At the beginning, a slide shows a protest with a woman holding a black sign that reads "END VIOLENCE AGAINST WOMEN" in white letters; other partial signs read "ABUSE OF POWER" and "MISOGYNY." The image also includes license details for the photo. Next, the slide transitions to another protest image with two signs; one reads "SILENT + FORGOTTEN NO MORE" in yellow and red, and the other states "JUSTICE FOR MISSING & MURDERED ABORIGINAL WOMEN" in red and black on a cardboard sign. Subsequently, a screenshot of a HuffPost article appears with the headline "Violence Against Women Canada: 67% Of Canadians Know A Woman Who Has Experienced Abuse," indicating a significant societal issue. This is followed by a geographical map titled "Calgary’s Domestic Violence Hot Spots," displaying highlighted areas in green and red to indicate concentrations of domestic violence, with accompanying source information from CBC News and a Twitter handle. Finally, a meme features Winifred Sanderson from Hocus Pocus on the phone, with the caption "MY FACE WHEN CHILDREN DON’T HAVE ACCESS TO COMPREHENSIVE SEX-ED," as the speaker points towards it, signaling a transition in her discussion.

A woman with curly brown hair, wearing glasses, a black top, and a patterned scarf, stands behind a podium, speaking and gesturing expressively with her hands throughout the segment. Her background is a stylized cityscape with glowing yellow and blue elements. As she speaks, five different slides are shown on the right side of the screen. The first slide (00:00-00:04) is a meme featuring the character Winifred Sanderson from Hocus Pocus, with text that reads: "MY FACE WHEN CHILDREN DON'T HAVE ACCESS TO COMPREHENSIVE SEX-ED". The second slide (00:04-00:24) displays a protest banner held by people in a street, with "MY BODY MY CHOICE" in English on the left (accompanied by a magnifying glass containing a feminist fist symbol) and "MON CORPS MON CHOIX" (My Body My Choice) in French on the right (accompanied by a pink heart). Below the magnifying glass, smaller text reads "STOP MURDERING CHILDREN". The third slide (00:24-00:43) is an exterior photograph of a large, modern building with a glass facade, labeled "CALGARY MUNICIPAL PLAZA". The fourth slide (00:43-01:03) shows an industrial landscape with multiple smoking chimneys under a blue sky, identified as "Fort McMurray Oil Sands". The final slide (01:03-01:13) is a graphic illustrating a line of identical gray, faceless human figures, with one golden, female-coded figure breaking away from the line and walking in a different direction. All photo slides include attribution and creative commons license information.

In this video segment, a woman with short, curly, dark hair and glasses is positioned in the lower-left corner, speaking into a microphone at a podium. She is wearing a black top and a patterned scarf, and her hands are actively gesturing as she talks. Behind her, a projected image of a blue-hued cityscape with illuminated buildings serves as the backdrop. In the upper-right portion of the screen, a graphic initially displays a long line of gray, stylized human figures, with one gold figure stepping out of the line and walking forward, symbolizing individual departure or leadership. After a transition, this graphic is replaced by a photograph of a smiling blonde woman in a white blazer waving to a crowd, with several other people applauding and standing behind her, and a large building in the background. The speaker continues to gesture and speak, raising her hand high to emphasize her points, while the image of the waving woman remains on screen.

The video displays a split screen throughout. On the bottom left, a woman with curly brown hair, glasses, a black top, and a black patterned scarf is seen speaking into a microphone while standing at a wooden podium. She initially raises her right arm in a gesture before lowering it and looking down at her notes. The background behind her is a blurry cityscape with red and orange lighting. On the top right, a photograph is first shown of a smiling blonde woman in a white jacket and navy top, waving to a group of people who are clapping and smiling, with a large stone building in the background. This image then transitions to a visual metaphor: a white background with a pencil eraser actively rubbing out the "in-" prefix from the word "inequality," leaving only the word "equality." The speaker mentions "universal basic income" and "a progressive tax structure." A brief, high-pitched metallic sound is heard at the end of the segment.

A woman with glasses and dark hair tied back, wearing a black top and scarf, stands at a podium with a microphone, speaking animatedly and using broad hand gestures. From 0:03, a graphic appears on the right side of the screen, showing a grey pencil erasing the "in" from the word "inequality" against a white background, leaving "equality" with red eraser shavings visible. As the woman continues to speak passionately, moving her hands to emphasize her points, the graphic changes at 0:14 to a black rectangle with white text that reads "got privilege?", framed by a white background. The woman gestures by patting her stomach, pointing, and holding her hands open. At 0:33, the graphic changes again, displaying a collage of colorful logos on a white background. These logos represent various organizations, including "ALBERTA NETWORK OF IMMIGRANT WOMEN," "ccasa," "CIWA," "CANADIAN WOMEN'S FOUNDATION," "Calgary Women's Emergency Shelter," "YWCA CALGARY," "WINS WOMEN IN NEED SOCIETY," "Awo Taan Healing Lodge Society," "shift value for women's equality," and "ask her." The woman concludes her statement, still using expressive hand movements, as the video ends.

In this video segment, a woman with dark curly hair and glasses, dressed in a black top and a patterned scarf, stands at a podium with a microphone. She actively speaks, gesturing with both hands to emphasize her points. Behind her, the background is an abstract, colorful representation of a city skyline at night. On the right side of the screen, against a white background, are multiple logos of various women's organizations. These include "ALBERTA NETWORK OF IMMIGRANT WOMEN," "ccasa," "CIWA," "CANADIAN WOMEN'S FOUNDATION," "Calgary Women's Emergency Shelter," "YWCA CALGARY," "WINS WOMEN IN NEED SOCIETY," "Awo Taan Healing Lodge Society," "shift," and "ask her." Around the 0:14 mark, these logos disappear, and the right side of the screen becomes black, displaying white text that reads: "Gender justice is long overdue." The woman continues to speak and gesture with conviction throughout the segment.

In this video segment, a woman with dark curly hair, glasses, and a black top with a black scarf speaks at a podium. She is gesturing with her hands while delivering a speech. From 0:05 to 0:11, white text on the right side of the dark screen reads "Gender justice is long overdue," which she articulates at the end of her sentence. The background behind her features abstract, colorful shapes. As she finishes speaking around 0:11, the screen transitions, and a graphic appears on the right, displaying "PechaKucha Night CALGARY 20x20 IMAGES SECONDS" (20x20 images seconds) and "EVENT #35 OVERDUE" (Event #35 Overdue) in a vintage-style font, with "In partnership with ROCKETHOUSE & CALGARY PUBLIC LIBRARY" (In partnership with Rockethouse & Calgary Public Library) below it. The audience erupts in applause and cheers as the woman smiles, looking at them. From 0:16, more white text overlays the graphic: "Join the newsletter, suggest a speaker, or sign up to volunteer for PechaKucha Calgary at: WWW.PKNYYC.com" (Join the newsletter, suggest a speaker, or sign up to volunteer for PechaKucha Calgary at: www.pknyyc.com). The applause continues until 0:21 when the screen abruptly turns black.
